reuse.why: The API and existing planning consumers reuse getScheduledAmount, which also reuses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance definition.

duplication.why: Range selection and approximate-amount arithmetic remain centralized rather than being repeated across consumers.

placement.why: Expected-amount policy stays in shared schedules code, while API serialization and consumer-specific data extraction remain in their established layers.

scope.why: The edits address schedule amount policy, its consumers, API exposure, tests, and release documentation.

maintainability.why: The optional string operator behind a positional boolean makes policy inputs easy to omit, as computeSchedulePreviewTransactions still does, and overlapping release notes describe superseded policies.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Changed consumers use getScheduledAmount rather than implementing expected-amount policy themselves.

disguised_duplication.where: The diff shares policy arithmetic directly and introduces no reshaped copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount replaces rangeRounding with amountOp and adds an isapprox conditional; no call site independently reimplements the policy.
